media:group.media:title: TU Delft - Master track Signals, Networking and Sensing
media:group.media:description:
Signals, Networking and Sensing | MSc Electrical Engineering at TU Delft
What happens when signals, networks and sensing technologies come together? Discover the new Signals, Networking and Sensing (SNS) track within the MSc Electrical Engineering at TU Delft.
The track focuses on three key areas: 🔹 Signal Processing – turning complex data into useful information 🔹 Network Science – understanding and analysing complex networks 🔹 Radar Systems – developing advanced technologies for sensing and detection
SNS brings together these disciplines to prepare students for the development of future technologies in electrical engineering, communications and sensing.
In this video, we take a closer look at the new track, what you will learn and how it prepares you for the challenges and opportunities of tomorrow.
👉 Learn more about the MSc Signals, Networking and Sensing: https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/masters/ee/msc-electrical-engineering/programme/tracks/track-signals-networks-sensing

entry.title: BSc Health and Technology | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: BSc Health and Technology | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
De zorg staat onder druk: wachttijden lopen op, zorgkosten blijven stijgen en het tekort aan personeel wordt steeds voelbaarder. Tegelijkertijd biedt nieuwe technologie kansen om de zorg anders te organiseren en te verbeteren. In onze nieuwe Bacheloropleiding Health and Technology werk je in een team aan complexe zorgvraagstukken. Samen ontwerp en analyseer je technologische én organisatorische oplossingen die bijdragen aan een toekomstbestendig zorgsysteem.
Je leert hoe je complexe uitdagingen in de zorg vanuit verschillende perspectieven kunt aanpakken. Je combineert kennis van de zorg met design, data, AI, modelling en biomedical engineering. Samen met zorgprofessionals, onderzoekers en andere disciplines ontwerp en integreer je slimme oplossingen voor de zorg van morgen.
Deze TU Delft opleiding start in september 2027 in het Erasmus MC in Rotterdam en is ontwikkeld door TU Delft, Erasmus MC en Erasmus University Rotterdam.
Meer informatie over de bacheloropleiding: https://www.tudelft.nl/bsc/ht
Wil je ontdekken of Health and Technology bij jou past? Kijk hier voor meer informatie over studiekeuzeactiviteiten: https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/studievoorlichting/voorlichting-bachelor/

media:group.media:title: 183rd Dies Natalis TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
Making sense of mobility is the theme for our 183rd Dies Natalis celebrations. Mobility is a wicked problem: complex and interconnected, affecting climate change, social equity and urban health. We are at a critical juncture, and the future depends on the choices we make today. The way forward isn't straightforward. It is a journey through complex dilemmas and inevitable trade-offs. The challenges we face require new knowledge, bold decisions and adaptive thinking – recognising that every solution has consequences, and every progress comes at a cost.
Yet within these complexities lies an opportunity. By embracing tough choices and working together, we can steer towards a more sustainable, just and resilient future. So join us on Thursday 16 January, and throughout the Mobility Week programme, to shape the future of mobility together.

entry.title: Opening Academic Year 2026-2027 - Nature Inspires, Inspire Your Nature

media:group.media:title: Opening Academic Year 2026-2027 - Nature Inspires, Inspire Your Nature
media:group.media:description:
Zoals een zaadje zijn weg vindt naar het licht, zo begint elke ontwikkeling met nieuwsgierigheid. Met een vraag, een ontmoeting, een idee dat langzaam vorm krijgt.
TU Delft is een plek waar mensen samenkomen om te groeien. Waar kennis wortel schiet, perspectieven elkaar kruisen en nieuwe mogelijkheden ontstaan. Een gemeenschap die voortdurend in beweging is, gevoed door verbeeldingskracht, lef en de wil om bij te dragen aan een betere wereld.
Met het thema “Nature Inspires / Inspire your nature” vieren we de kracht van groei in al haar vormen. De natuur herinnert ons eraan dat ontwikkeling geen rechte lijn is, maar een reis van ontdekken, verbinden en vernieuwen. Ze nodigt ons uit stil te staan bij wat ons inspireert en bij de unieke bijdrage die ieder van ons kan leveren.
Aan het begin van dit nieuwe academische jaar openen we samen een nieuw hoofdstuk. Laat je verrassen door nieuwe inzichten, ontmoet elkaar en vind inspiratie in de mensen en ideeën om je heen.
_________
Just as a seed finds its way towards the light, every journey of growth begins with curiosity. With a question, an encounter, an idea slowly taking shape.
TU Delft is a place where people come together to grow. Where knowledge takes root, perspectives intersect, and new possibilities emerge. A community in constant motion, nourished by imagination, courage, and the desire to contribute to a better world.
With the theme “Nature Inspires / Inspire your nature”, we celebrate the power of growth in all its forms. Nature reminds us that development is rarely a straight line, but a journey of discovery, connection, and renewal. It invites us to reflect on what inspires us and on the unique contribution each of us can make.
At the start of this new academic year, we open a new chapter together. Be inspired by fresh insights, connect with others, and discover inspiration in the people and ideas around you.
Speakers
Ingrid Thijssen
Driven by her belief in the power of technology and talent development, Ingrid Thijssen is committed to finding solutions to the major societal challenges of our time. As President of TU Delft’s Executive Board, she stresses the importance of curiosity, innovation and engineering, with nature increasingly serving as a source of inspiration for new technological breakthroughs.
Hester Bijl
Driven by the belief that technological progress and social impact are inextricably linked, Hester Bijl is dedicated to education and research that has a real impact. As Rector Magnificus of TU Delft, she inspires a new generation of engineers to think curiously, push boundaries and act responsibly while considering the challenges facing a sustainable society.
Wopke Hoekstra
Since 2023, Wopke Hoekstra has been the European Commissioner for Climate, Net Zero and Clean Growth, and has been formally responsible for achieving the European climate targets. In this capacity, he has been dedicated to implementing the European Green Deal and realising a carbon-neutral European Union by 2050.
Elvin Karana
While the world searches for sustainable alternatives to polluting production methods, Professor Elvin Karana is exploring new avenues. From the BioDesign Lab, Professor Karana, a professor of materials innovation and design, is developing living materials that could help strike a better balance between humans and the ecosystem.
Josefien Groot
Driven by her belief that people and nature can coexist in greater harmony, Josefien Groot is committed to bringing about sustainable change. As cofounder and Chair of the Board of Qlayers, she develops environmentally friendly painting robots that contribute to cleaner industrial processes. Furthermore, inspired by her passion for self-sufficient living, she is exploring what a more sustainable lifestyle might entail. (See Alumnus of the Year 2025)
Marjolein van Esch
Driven by the ambition to keep cities livable in a changing climate, Marjolein van Esch explores how science and design can contribute to effective climate adaptation, with nature-based solutions playing a key role. As Academic Lead for Climate Change Adaptation at the TU Delft Climate Action Programme, she is committed to fostering interdisciplinary collaboration and developing solutions that prepare cities for the future.
Vera Kortman
Vera Kortman is fascinated by the ingenious solutions that nature has developed over millions of years and is investigating how these principles can be applied to new technology. She is, for example, working on soft, mechanically intelligent robots inspired by organisms such as octopuses.
Austin Lopez
Austin Lopez is intrigued by the ingenious ways in which insects move through their environment. He is working on the next generation of flying robots. His drones draw their sensory capabilities and flight behaviour from nature and possess the collective intelligence of insect swarms.

entry.title: The future of traffic: connected, coordinated and secure | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: The future of traffic: connected, coordinated and secure | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
At TU Delft Mechanical Engineering, scientists are exploring how automated vehicles can travel together in closely coordinated groups, known as platoons.
By communicating and responding to each other's actions, vehicles in a platoon can improve traffic flow, increase safety, and make transportation more efficient. The researchers also study how to protect these connected systems from malicious cyber attacks, helping ensure that future automated vehicles remain safe, reliable, and resilient.
The team tests platooning and cybersecurity strategies using small car like robots equipped with onboard sensors. These robots allow researchers to develop and validate new approaches before applying them to real world vehicles.
🚗 More Transport & Mobility Research https://edu.nl/fqv89 🤖 Related Master’s programme Robotics https://edu.nl/wwwr7

media:group.media:title: Bachelor Technische Natuurkunde | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
Wil je weten hoe protonen kunnen worden gebruikt om mensen te genezen? Of hoe je betere zonnecellen kunt maken? Bij Technische Natuurkunde aan de TU Delft vind je antwoorden op dit soort vragen.
‘Technische Natuurkunde’ is niet alleen gericht op een goed begrip van de fundamentele natuurkunde, maar ook op het toepassen in dagelijkse en minder dagelijkse dingen. Je duikt bij TN in de techniek vanuit een solide basis in de wis- en natuurkunde: van fundamenteel (mechanica, elektromagnetisme, kwantummechanica) tot toegepast (stromingsleer, elektronica, signalen).
De bacheloropleiding is breed opgezet zodat je kennis maakt met uiteenlopende aspecten van zowel de klassieke, de moderne als de toegepaste natuurkunde, het natuurkundig ontwerpen en de wiskunde. De opleiding is een mix van hoorcolleges, werkcolleges, practica, projecten in kleine groepen en begeleide zelfstudie.
Meer informatie over de opleiding: https://edu.nl/73m4n

entry.title: How comfortable should autonomous driving feel? | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: How comfortable should autonomous driving feel? | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
At TU Delft Mechanical Engineering, researchers use the Delft Advanced Driving Simulator (DAVSi) to study how people experience future mobility systems.
The simulator combines realistic vehicle controls, immersive visuals, and a motion platform that recreates sensations such as acceleration, braking, and cornering. This allows researchers to investigate how automated driving behaviour affects passenger comfort, trust, and acceptance.
DAVSi is equipped with advanced measurement systems, including eye tracking and physiological sensors, enabling researchers to better understand how people respond physically and mentally to automated driving. The insights help engineers design vehicles that are not only safe, but also comfortable and enjoyable to use.
From automated driving and human machine interaction to biomechanics and user experience, DAVSi supports research that is helping shape the future of mobility.

entry.title: How one bike is helping build smarter cities | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: How one bike is helping build smarter cities | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
Researchers at TU Delft Mechanical Engineering have developed the SenseBike: a bicycle equipped with advanced sensors similar to those used in autonomous vehicles, including cameras, lidar, GPS, and inertial measurement systems.
By cycling through urban environments, the SenseBike creates detailed real time maps of city streets and gathers unique data about cyclist behaviour. This information helps improve the perception algorithms used in automated vehicles and supports the design of safer infrastructure and intersections for cyclists.
The SenseBike was developed by Holger Caesar, Jason Moore and students Jan Peter Simons and Denniz Goren.

entry.title: Improving remote driving for safer autonomous vehicles | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: Improving remote driving for safer autonomous vehicles | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
Automated vehicles perform well in many situations, but what happens when they encounter unexpected environments or severe weather conditions?
Researchers at TU Delft Mechanical Engineering are investigating teleoperation as a human fallback solution for automated driving. Georgios Papaioannou and his team have developed an advanced remote driving system to study how operators can safely and effectively take control when needed.
Their research focuses on creating a realistic driving experience for remote operators by improving the transmission of essential cues, including visual and haptic feedback, helping to make remote vehicle control safer and more intuitive.
🚗 Discover more Transport & Mobility Research https://edu.nl/fqv89 🤖 Related Master’s programme Robotics https://edu.nl/wwwr7

entry.title: Designing new Satellite Technologies for monitoring Biodiversity | TU Delft

media:group.media:title: Designing new Satellite Technologies for monitoring Biodiversity | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
To track the status of Biodiversity conservation and restoration effects, new satellite remote sensing technologies are required. To this purpose, the Quantative and Terrestrial Remote Sensing (QUARTS) lab and the Space instrumentation Laboratory at the TU Delft have joint forces to explore how Spectro-Polarimetry can be used for leaf inclination distribution functions, an essential biodiversity variables that so far has remained illusive.
To explore how such satellite technology could be used for additional research, 16 students from both Civil Engineering and Geoscience and Aerospace Engineering participated in a Talent Hackathon (organised at the Amsterdam Space Symposium) to design a mission based on spectro-polarimetry.
With expert guidance from experts from the TU Delft, Leiden University, Erasmus University and SRON, 3 distinct mission concepts were created and pitched to space entrepeneurs at the ASS2026.

entry.title: TU Delft - Student Story - MSc Earth, Climate and Technology - Exploring Earth's Hidden Heat

media:group.media:title: TU Delft - Student Story - MSc Earth, Climate and Technology - Exploring Earth's Hidden Heat
media:group.media:description:
In this video you see TU Delft's MSc student Faye. For her studies in Earth, Climate and Technology, see traveled to the Alsace region in France, one of Europe's most geothermally active areas. Here, she set out a thermal drone mission to measure thermal anomalies on the ground surface, which could be indicative of geothermal activities.
"If we can detect surface temperature anomalies in our drone-derived data, then this approach could be used all over the world in other regions to see if those locations could also be used for creating geothermal reservoirs".

media:group.media:title: Navigating autonomous vessels | TU Delft
media:group.media:description:
At the Researchlab Autonomous Shipping, scientists test how vessels can operate without direct human control. Using a fleet of sensor equipped model ships, they experiment with navigation, obstacle avoidance and interaction among multiple vessels.
The lab combines indoor facilities such as towing and flume tanks with outdoor test locations, creating a unique environment where new technologies can be developed and validated in increasingly complex conditions.
This research helps bridge the gap between simulations and real world applications, accelerating the development of autonomous shipping and more efficient use of waterways.
